title: Like Their Parents, Not the Same: Parent Guide
pageTitle: Like Their Parents, Not the Same
endLine: Offspring are like their parents, but not identical.

scenes.tts: Are all the peas in a pod the same size? They can look like a row of twins. A ruler can help your child look for differences.
scenes.caption: Are all the peas in a pod the same size? They can look like a row of twins. A ruler can help your child look for differences.
scenes.visual: Open on a schematic overhead kitchen table. A green pod sits on a white paper plate under the question 'All the same?' The pod cracks open to show a row of peas without highlighting any size differences.
scenes.narration: Are all the peas in a pod the same size? They can look like a row of twins. A ruler can help your child look for differences.

scenes.visual: Same table and open pod stay in place. The title 'Like Their Parents, Not the Same' appears above the plate while the peas rock very slightly.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea your child will find. Offspring, the young a living thing makes, are like their parents, but not identical. Along the way, your child practices looking closely, measuring, and sorting. It takes about thirty minutes.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea your child will find. Offspring, the young a living thing makes, are like their parents, but not identical. Along the way, your child practices looking closely, measuring, and sorting. It takes about thirty minutes.
scenes.visual: Same table. A simple drawn pea plant appears at the top edge, with a soft arrow down to the row of peas on the plate. Label near the arrow: 'Offspring: alike, not identical'. Then three short labels appear one by one beside the plate: 'Look closely', 'Measure', 'Same or different'. A small clock icon reads '30 minutes'.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea your child will find. Offspring, the young a living thing makes, are like their parents, but not identical. Along the way, your child practices looking closely, measuring, and sorting. It takes about thirty minutes.

scenes.tts: Set out three or four pea pods from the store, an apple, and a sweet bell pepper. Add a ruler, paper plate, pencil, cutting board, knife, and animal family pictures. Set out five or six leaves from one tree or shrub you know is safe to touch.
scenes.caption: Set out three or four pea pods from the store, an apple, and a sweet bell pepper. Add a ruler, paper plate, pencil, cutting board, knife, and animal family pictures. Set out five or six leaves from one tree or shrub you know is safe to touch.
scenes.visual: On the kitchen table, show the grocery produce, then the paper plate, ruler and pencil. An adult sets down the board and knife out of the child's reach. Show a close-up of similar leaves from one branch, then an open picture book with a cat and kittens.
scenes.narration: Set out three or four pea pods from the store, an apple, and a sweet bell pepper. Add a ruler, paper plate, pencil, cutting board, knife, and animal family pictures. Set out five or six leaves from one tree or shrub you know is safe to touch.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child throughout. You do all the cutting. Peas and seeds are choking hazards for children under four. Keep them out of reach, and call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep leaves and seeds out of mouths.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child throughout. You do all the cutting. Peas and seeds are choking hazards for children under four. Keep them out of reach, and call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep leaves and seeds out of mouths.
scenes.visual: Show an adult hand beside a child's hand at the plate. Show the adult moving a bowl of peas and seeds out of reach, then a phone with 'Choking: call 911'. End on a crossed-out mouth beside a leaf and a seed.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child throughout. You do all the cutting. Peas and seeds are choking hazards for children under four. Keep them out of reach, and call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep leaves and seeds out of mouths.

scenes.tts: Check for pea, peanut, apple, or pepper allergies first. A child with an allergy can watch while you handle the samples. Use a sweet bell pepper. Skip hot peppers. Wash the produce and everyone's hands. Keep activity samples out of mouths.
scenes.caption: Check for pea, peanut, apple, or pepper allergies first. A child with an allergy can watch while you handle the samples. Use a sweet bell pepper. Skip hot peppers. Wash the produce and everyone's hands. Keep activity samples out of mouths.
scenes.visual: Show produce and soapy hands in turn. An adult moves the washed samples to the activity plate. Use the short label 'Samples, not snacks'.
scenes.narration: Check for pea, peanut, apple, or pepper allergies first. A child with an allergy can watch while you handle the samples. Use a sweet bell pepper. Skip hot peppers. Wash the produce and everyone's hands. Keep activity samples out of mouths.

scenes.tts: Start before you open anything. Hold up a closed pod and ask, 'Will the peas inside all be the same?' Write down your child's guess. You will check it together soon.
scenes.caption: Start before you open anything. Hold up a closed pod and ask, 'Will the peas inside all be the same?' Write down your child's guess. You will check it together soon.
scenes.visual: A drawn adult hand holds up a closed pea pod over the table. A speech bubble appears: 'Will they all be the same?' A small notepad slides in at the corner and a pencil writes a short line on it, marked 'Our guess'.
scenes.narration: Start before you open anything. Hold up a closed pod and ask, 'Will the peas inside all be the same?' Write down your child's guess. You will check it together soon.

scenes.tts: Let your child split each pod with their thumbs. Line up the peas from one pod on the plate, in the order they sat. Count those peas, then count the peas in another pod. The numbers often differ.
scenes.caption: Let your child split each pod with their thumbs. Line up the peas from one pod on the plate, in the order they sat. Count those peas, then count the peas in another pod. The numbers often differ.
scenes.visual: Two small drawn thumbs press a pod open along its seam. The peas roll out and settle into a straight row on the plate, keeping pod order. Simple number tags pop up under each pea. A second pod opens beside it with a different count of peas, and both totals appear in large type.
scenes.narration: Let your child split each pod with their thumbs. Line up the peas from one pod on the plate, in the order they sat. Count those peas, then count the peas in another pod. The numbers often differ.

scenes.tts: Now a question for you. The peas look like twins. When you lay them next to a ruler, what do you expect to see?
scenes.caption: Now a question for you. The peas look like twins. When you lay them next to a ruler, what do you expect to see?
scenes.visual: The row of peas sits beside a drawn ruler, not yet aligned. A high-contrast question card on the left reads: 'Next to a ruler, what will you see?'
scenes.narration: Now a question for you. The peas look like twins. When you lay them next to a ruler, what do you expect to see?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the row of peas. Keep slow ambient motion: the peas rock very slightly and a soft light drifts across the plate, without revealing any sizes.

scenes.tts: Measure each pea across. Most garden peas are about one centimeter, or a little smaller. Your child finds the biggest, the smallest, and any that are paler or flat. Then go back to the guess. Ask, 'What did the ruler show?'
scenes.caption: Measure each pea across. Most garden peas are about one centimeter, or a little smaller. Your child finds the biggest, the smallest, and any that are paler or flat. Then go back to the guess. Ask, 'What did the ruler show?'
scenes.visual: The ruler slides under the row of peas. Gentle highlight rings mark one bigger pea, one paler pea and one tiny flat pea, each with a short label: 'Bigger', 'Paler', 'Tiny and flat'. The notepad with 'Our guess' slides back in and a check-and-question mark appears beside it.
scenes.narration: Measure each pea across. Most garden peas are about one centimeter, or a little smaller. Your child finds the biggest, the smallest, and any that are paler or flat. Then go back to the guess. Ask, 'What did the ruler show?'

scenes.tts: All these peas came from one plant. A bigger pea from this pod had the same parent plant as a smaller one. Much of the difference comes from how much food reached each pea as it grew.
scenes.caption: All these peas came from one plant. A bigger pea from this pod had the same parent plant as a smaller one. Much of the difference comes from how much food reached each pea as it grew.
scenes.visual: Show one drawn pea plant and one pod. Bring a larger and smaller pea from that pod side by side beside the ruler. Label the pod 'One parent plant'.
scenes.narration: All these peas came from one plant. A bigger pea from this pod had the same parent plant as a smaller one. Much of the difference comes from how much food reached each pea as it grew.

scenes.tts: Cut the apple across its middle to reveal a star of seed pockets. Cut the pepper from top to bottom. Line up five seeds from each and compare their sizes and shapes. Compare the leaves, then measure the longest and shortest.
scenes.caption: Cut the apple across its middle to reveal a star of seed pockets. Cut the pepper from top to bottom. Line up five seeds from each and compare their sizes and shapes. Compare the leaves, then measure the longest and shortest.
scenes.visual: On a steady cutting board, show an adult knife cut across the apple and lengthwise through the pepper. An adult hand holds the fruit with fingers curled away from the blade. Show two rows of five seeds, then lay out leaves from one branch and measure the longest and shortest.
scenes.narration: Cut the apple across its middle to reveal a star of seed pockets. Cut the pepper from top to bottom. Line up five seeds from each and compare their sizes and shapes. Compare the leaves, then measure the longest and shortest.

scenes.tts: Show kittens with their mother and ask, 'How are they alike?' Then show a caterpillar and a butterfly. Sort the pictures together. Put babies that look like their parents in one group and babies that look different at first in another.
scenes.caption: Show kittens with their mother and ask, 'How are they alike?' Then show a caterpillar and a butterfly. Sort the pictures together. Put babies that look like their parents in one group and babies that look different at first in another.
scenes.visual: Open the picture book to kittens with their mother and a caterpillar beside a butterfly. Slide copies of the illustrations onto two areas of the table labeled 'Look alike at first' and 'Look different at first'.
scenes.narration: Show kittens with their mother and ask, 'How are they alike?' Then show a caterpillar and a butterfly. Sort the pictures together. Put babies that look like their parents in one group and babies that look different at first in another.

scenes.tts: Keep the talk to plants and animals. Do not ask which parent your child looks like. Many children are adopted, fostered, or live in blended families, and the question can hurt.
scenes.caption: Keep the talk to plants and animals. Do not ask which parent your child looks like. Many children are adopted, fostered, or live in blended families, and the question can hurt.
scenes.visual: The picture book closes gently and the plate of peas returns to the center. A short label sits above it: 'Plants and animals only'.
scenes.narration: Keep the talk to plants and animals. Do not ask which parent your child looks like. Many children are adopted, fostered, or live in blended families, and the question can hurt.

scenes.tts: Return to your child's guess and have them show you what they noticed. Count the peas and seeds and clear the table. Wash everyone's hands again. Peas from one pod can be alike in some ways and differ in others.
scenes.caption: Return to your child's guess and have them show you what they noticed. Count the peas and seeds and clear the table. Wash everyone's hands again. Peas from one pod can be alike in some ways and differ in others.
scenes.visual: Return to the measured peas beside the ruler. A child's hand points to two peas. An adult gathers the samples and clears the table. Show soapy hands, then return to a simple drawing of the pea row.
scenes.narration: Return to your child's guess and have them show you what they noticed. Count the peas and seeds and clear the table. Wash everyone's hands again. Peas from one pod can be alike in some ways and differ in others.

scenes.line: Offspring are like their parents, but not identical.
scenes.visual: Clean warm end card with a faint row of peas beside a ruler in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Offspring are like their parents, but not identical.'
